text: Balendra Shah, commonly known as Balen, was born on 27 April 1990 in Naradevi, Kathmandu, to a Maithili Madhesi family; his parents are Late Ram Narayan Shah, an Ayurvedic practitioner, and Dhruvadevi Shah, who moved to Kathmandu from Mahottari District after his father’s posting at Naradevi Ayurvedic Hospital. Shah pursued his 10+2 education at V.S. Niketan Higher Secondary School and earned a bachelor’s degree (BE) in civil engineering from Himalayan Whitehouse International College, followed by a master’s degree (MTech) in structural engineering from Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) in Karnataka, India. He is currently pursuing a PhD in Civil Engineering at Kathmandu University, supported by a KU Researcher's Fellowship, with a research focus on "Conservation of Newa Heritage Structure to promote Tourism and Economy." From an early age, Shah showed interest in music and poetry, releasing his first single, Sadak Balak, in 2012 during his ninth grade, and gaining prominence in 2013 through his appearance on the YouTube battle rap series Raw Barz. In July 2022, he drew controversy for using a sacred crown in Nephopko Shreepech, a hip-hop reality show he judged. As mayor, Shah introduced live telecasts of municipal council meetings, initiated garbage disposal from 7 June 2022 through an agreement with the Ministry of Urban Development, and directed private companies to manage uncollected solid waste in August 2022. He also ordered the demolition of private properties above the Tukucha River to uncover it, leading to a writ petition and an interim court order halting the demolition. Shah requested the removal of unauthorized police sub-stations on sidewalks and clashed with the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal over the removal of unapproved construction materials at Tribhuvan International Airport, resulting in a legal dispute and a high court stay. His office issued a 7-day public notice to evict landless squatters on riverbanks, leading to clashes, injuries, and a subsequent complaint from the Home Ministry, which escalated tensions with the federal government, culminating in the suspension of garbage collection from Singha Durbar. Shah has faced criticism from Human Rights Watch and social activists for using disproportionate force against street vendors, with videos circulating of police chasing, beating, and confiscating vendor properties, which critics argue harms the urban poor. In September 2023, activist Iih stood for 199 hours outside Kathmandu City Hall, demanding vendor rights, supported by figures including Gagan Thapa, Kamal Thapa, and Surendra Pandey; Shah responded by citing existing laws and expressed concern over confiscated properties, leading to an agreement on temporary permits, return of goods, and an alternative plan. Shah is known for his confrontational style, including removing illegal buildings, uncovering the Tukucha River, and clearing street vendors. In 2023, he placed a map of Greater Nepal in his office—a symbolic act interpreted as a response to the “Akhanda Bharat” mural in India’s new Parliament building, which some in Nepal saw as depicting Nepali territory as part of undivided India. This action drew strong objections from India. He also temporarily banned the screening of Indian films after Adipurush included the line “Sita is the daughter of India,” a claim disputed in Nepal where Sita is traditionally believed to have been born in Janakpur; despite a court order to remove the ban, Shah initially refused, prompting a contempt of court petition before allowing screenings to resume. During the Gen-Z Protests, the Nepal Student Union filed a police complaint accusing Shah of inciting violence against heritage sites, though he denied the claims, stating city teams worked continuously to ensure safety. Shah is a supporter of the irredentist Greater Nepal theory, which claims territories beyond Nepal’s current borders, including areas now in Indian states, that were once under Nepalese control before the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli. He was elected mayor on 26 May 2022 with 38.6% of the votes, defeating Nepali Congress candidate Sirjana Shrestha and CPN (UML) candidate Keshav Sthapit by a margin of over 23,000 votes, becoming the first independent candidate to hold the office. He was sworn in on 30 May 2022 and served until his resignation on 18 January 2026. He is currently contesting in the upcoming general elections as a candidate for the Prime Minister of Nepal and joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) in late 2025. Shah is married to Sabina Kafle, a public health professional, and lives in Gairigaun, Tinkune. His campaign emphasized waste management, road traffic control, public service delivery, anti-corruption, and cultural heritage preservation. TIME Magazine included him in its 'The 100 emerging leaders who are shaping the future' list in 2023.
